messages:
anya: quick alert — local NVMe write latency spike in us-west2 is preventing ~20 GPU attaches, backlog climbing fast :grimacing:
ops-bot: [ALERT] metric=nvme_write_latency region=us-west2 nodes=gnode-uw2-{101,103,107,110} current=34ms threshold=25ms
ben: are these kubelet attach errors or underlying nvme firmware noise? logs?
anya: mostly kubelet AttachVolume timeouts and a handful of 'nvme0: I/O CRC error' lines in dmesg. saw a big cleaner sweep at 03:12 UTC against ephemeral label=cleanup=true
rahul: ok can we pause the cleaner waves for that cohort? last month we saw the same pattern when janitor did large deletes
claire: agree. i'm uncomfortable with full pause, suggest immediate concurrency drop + smaller delete chunk size
anya: doing both. patching env: CLEANER_PARALLELISM=3 and MAX_DELETE_BYTES=536870912 for nodes matching region=us-west2 and label ephemeral=cleanup
ben: paste the command?
anya: ran:
```
kubectl -n infra set env daemonset/ephemeral-cleaner CLEANER_PARALLELISM=3 --context=us-west2
kubectl -n infra set env daemonset/ephemeral-cleaner MAX_DELETE_BYTES=536870912 --context=us-west2
```
rahul: nice. also flip cleaner to backoff-on-attach=true if available so it yields to attach-critical ops
claire: added a temporary credit: cleaner.flags=yield_to_attach in the running daemonset (rolling update to 4 nodes)
ops-bot: [METRIC] us-west2 nvme_write_latency 1m=29ms 5m=31ms 15m=16ms\
anya: after throttling first wave, 1m latency dropped from 34ms -> 19ms. attach backlog reduced from 20 -> 6 in 10m
ben: estimate residual risk window? If this lingers we'll either delay non-critical GPU jobs or shift provisioning to eu-west1 which has spare capacity
rahul: rough ETA to clear current backlog ~40-75m depending on tail latency. prefer to avoid cross-region unless we see >30% attach failure rate sustained for 1h
claire: cost note: if we keep idle GPUs due to attaches, ballpark 50 gpu-minutes/hr wasted. tagging finance for precise $ calc later
anya: filing ticket INFRA-2184 "ephemeral-cleaner: attach-aware throttling and backoff" assigned to eng-infra. owners: rahul (lead), ben (rollback/playbook), anya (monitoring)
ben: playbook items: (1) quick throttle steps (what we ran), (2) attach-sensitive flag for cleaner, (3) canary deploy pattern for cleaner env updates
rahul: also add metric-driven auto-throttle: if nvme_write_latency > 25ms and attach_backlog > 5 then reduce parallelism to 2
ops-bot: [ACTION] Created INFRA-2184 with links to graphs and recent dmesg excerpts
anya: monitoring now. current nvme write latency 1m=18ms 5m=20ms and attach backlog 3. will wait 60m then close incident if stable
claire: follow-up: postmortem should consider safer default max_delete_bytes and a canary for cleaner wide rollouts
ben: agree. will prepare a short runbook snippet for oncall to handle similar spikes without whitelisting nodes manually
anya: thanks team, closing thread unless it regresses :thumbsup:
